name: Dust-Gale
description: Dust-Gale is a world defined by one thing: wind. The thin atmosphere, superheated by the scorching dayside and chilled by the frigid nights, drives gales that circle the planet in a continuous dust storm of varying intensity. The surface is a monotony of fine dust and exposed bedrock, scoured clean of any loose material larger than a grain of sand. Glass plains in the southern hemisphere, the remnants of some ancient cataclysmic event, have been sandblasted into opaque, frosted sheets.

The gales never truly stop, only vary between merely fierce and genuinely destructive. The dust reduces visibility to meters during the worst storms and creates a constant abrasive hiss against any surface. The temperature swings are brutal, with the thin atmosphere providing no thermal buffer between the searing day and the bitterly cold night. The canyons offer some shelter from the wind but concentrate the dust into choking density.

Radiation hotspots scattered across the glass plains suggest the cataclysm that created them may have been nuclear in nature, though whether through natural or artificial means remains debated. A graveyard of communications satellites orbits the planet, their systems degraded by decades of exposure to the dust that extends into the upper atmosphere. The satellites belonged to at least three different operators, suggesting the planet has attracted and defeated multiple attempts at development.

Dust-Gale's uranium deposits are significant and accessible, concentrated near the radiation hotspots in formations consistent with exposed ore bodies. The silicon in the glass plains is of exceptional purity and industrial value. But the relentless dust degrades equipment faster than it can be maintained, and the failed satellite constellation stands as testament to the planet's hostility. Any successful operation here will require engineering specifically designed to endure the endless grinding of Dust-Gale's wind.
